name: BSc Forensic Science
title: BSc Forensic Science
intro: The forensic science roadmap: admission, forensic biology, chemistry and crime-scene papers, lab training and careers in forensic labs and law enforcement.

phases.title: Class 11–12 subjects
phases.summary: Science with Physics, Chemistry and Biology (or Maths) is the usual requirement.
points: Most programmes need Class 12 Science with Chemistry and Biology or Physics.
Build strong chemistry and biology fundamentals and keen observation.
Read about forensic cases and the role of evidence in investigations.
Check the age and fitness requirements of institutes if you plan field roles.

phases.title: Entrance exams and admission
phases.summary: Institutes such as the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) use their own notified entrance tests, and others use CUET-UG or merit.
points: NFSU and some institutes conduct their own admission process; check each year’s notification.
CUET-UG is used by several central and state universities.
Choose colleges with forensic labs, internships with state forensic labs and police tie-ups.
Verify university recognition before paying fees.

phases.title: Year 1: foundation papers
phases.summary: Core science papers and lab skills.
points: Core papers: Introduction to Forensic Science, Forensic Physics, Forensic Chemistry and Biology Fundamentals.
Under NEP you also take language, environment and skill-enhancement courses.
Learn to maintain a lab notebook, follow safety rules and write practical reports.
Start reading beyond the syllabus and attend department seminars.

phases.title: Year 2–3: advanced and applied papers
phases.summary: Deeper papers, electives and a project.
points: Year 2: Forensic Biology and Serology, Toxicology, Fingerprints and Questioned Documents, and Criminal Law basics.
Year 3: Cyber Forensics, Forensic Ballistics, Crime Scene Management, DNA Fingerprinting, and a project or internship.
Complete a project or dissertation under a faculty guide.
Many universities offer a fourth Honours year with research.

phases.title: Lab skills, internships and training
points: Learn: evidence collection and preservation, fingerprint analysis, document examination, toxicology tests, DNA techniques and report writing for courts.
Do summer internships or short research projects in labs, companies and government institutions.
Take certificate courses on SWAYAM, NPTEL or industry bodies.
Keep a record of your projects, certificates and skills.

phases.title: After BSc: MSc, exams and careers
phases.summary: Master’s degree, NET/JRF, government jobs or industry.
points: Further study and careers: MSc Forensic Science, forensic scientist roles in Forensic Science Laboratories (FSL/CFSL), cyber forensics, police and private forensic firms.
Exams: NFSU and university entrances for MSc, CUET-PG, state FSL Scientific Officer recruitment and UGC NET.
Research route: MSc, then CSIR-UGC NET (JRF) or GATE and a PhD.
Government exams such as SSC and state PSCs are open to science graduates.
